evidence: app/package.json:8 — @gracile/gracile ^0.11.0, the latest stable but pre-1.0 framework (published ~6 months ago), underpins every page
app/package.json:16 — vite ^8.0.0, stable only since 2026-03-12 (Rolldown-based, major architecture change), used for the build
app/src/routes/(home).ts:1-2 — only documented stable Gracile APIs (defineRoute, server-html html); no experimental add-ons anywhere
app/src/client/interactions.ts:1 — interactivity is plain vanilla DOM, avoiding Gracile's experimental-phase CSR add-on documented at gracile.js.org/docs/learn/usage/output-modes
reach.rationale: No experimental APIs or flags are used, but the whole app necessarily rests on a very new pre-1.0 framework and a recently-stable Vite 8 — 'recently-stable APIs in central places' is exactly a 3.

evidence: app/server.mjs:1-16 — the entire Hono/Gracile integration surface is one small file mirroring the documented adapter example, trivially swappable
app/vite.config.js:1-9 — the only framework-specific config is a single gracile({ output: 'server' }) plugin entry
app/src/lib/api.ts:1 — data layer is plain fetch with an in-memory cache; no framework magic in the 15 source files
containment.rationale: Framework touchpoints are confined to server.mjs, the vite config, and route modules using standard conventions; there is nothing experimental spread through the code to contain.

evidence: app/vite.config.js:6 — output: 'server' is required by the spec (all data must be fetched over HTTP at request time, no build-time prerendering)
app/server.mjs:13-14 — honoAdapter is the documented path for server output; @gracile/gracile/hono is an official starter target
app/package.json:16 — vite ^8 sits inside Gracile's declared peer range (^7.0.0 || ^8.0.0) and Vite 7 is past regular-fix support, so it buys maintained support rather than novelty
app/src/document.client.ts:1 — chose plain JS over the experimental CSR/hydration path, i.e. the most stable option available
justification.rationale: Every framework touchpoint is either spec-mandated or the documented, most stable option; no use is gratuitous, and the experimental alternatives in the docs were deliberately avoided.

findings.issue: vite ^8.0.0 is the newest major (stable 2026-03-12) built on the Rolldown bundler swap; a future minor could surface behavior differences vs. the Vite 7 paths the framework was originally authored against
findings.suggestion: Keep vite pinned within Gracile's tested range and re-run the build after Vite minor upgrades; nothing else needed now since 8.x is the supported current release

findings.issue: @lit-labs/ssr ^4.0.0 (a 'labs' package) ships as a transitive dependency of @gracile/gracile — Lit SSR itself is still pre-stable branding
findings.suggestion: None required at the app level (the app never imports it); just be aware server-rendering internals could change across Gracile minors

findings.issue: The entire runtime depends on a pre-1.0 framework (0.11.0, ~115 weekly downloads, single maintainer), so minor releases may carry breaking changes
findings.suggestion: Pin the framework in package.json/package-lock to the exact 0.11.0 and upgrade deliberately; avoid 0.11.1-next prereleases

summary: The app contains zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs: it uses only Gracile's documented stable surface (defineRoute, server-html, the Hono adapter, output: 'server') and even avoids the framework's one explicitly experimental feature (the CSR add-on) in favor of vanilla progressive enhancement. The residual 'newness' is inherited — the mandated pre-1.0 framework itself and a recently-stable Vite 8 — both at their latest stable versions and correctly contained to server.mjs, the vite config, and standard route conventions. Risk of breakage is low and mostly external to this codebase.
